DESIGN.md:68: **Character:** Display type should feel engraved and authoritative without becoming medieval. Body type should feel contemporary, compact, and dependable. Contrast between them carries Essentia's hybrid identity more credibly than ornamental lettering.

Cube rules

Normal Magic rules apply unless this page says otherwise. Card text uses Yu-Gi-Oh! timing and identity inside Magic’s stack, zones, combat, and turn structure.

Setup and mulligan

This is a closed, high-power cube. Extra Deck cards—Fusion, Synchro, Xyz, and Link Creatures—start in the Sideboard, which represents the Extra Deck. Ritual Creatures remain in the Main Deck.

Cube mulligan

  1. Once before the game, choose any number of cards in your opening hand.
  2. Put those cards on the bottom of your Deck in any order.
  3. Draw the same number of cards. Do not shuffle.

Face-down creatures

  • Any creature may be cast face down for its normal cost.
  • Face down, it has no name, color, type, ability, power, or toughness.
  • It cannot be Flipped during the turn it enters. From the next turn, its controller may Flip it at sorcery speed.
  • A face-down creature may be Fusion or Ritual material, but not Synchro or Xyz material.
  • Flip triggers when the creature turns face up.

Trap cards

Trap is a supertype, such as Trap Instant orTrap Enchantment. A Trap cannot normally be cast from hand.

  1. Set it face down on the field as a special action. Setting does not use the stack, pay its casting cost, or count as a cast.
  2. While face down, it is a nameless, colorless, typeless nonland, noncreature permanent with no abilities or mana value.
  3. Starting on the following turn, turn it face up and cast it from the field at instant speed, paying normal costs. This uses the stack and counts as a cast from the field.
  4. Trap Instants and Sorceries go to Grave after resolving. Trap permanents enter face up. Explicit same-turn permission removes only the one-turn wait.

Special summons and the Extra Deck

  1. Set it face down on the field as a special action. Setting does not use the stack, pay its casting cost, or count as a cast.
  2. While face down, it is a nameless, colorless, typeless nonland, noncreature permanent with no abilities or mana value.
  3. Starting on the following turn, turn it face up and cast it from the field at instant speed, paying normal costs. This uses the stack and counts as a cast from the field.
  4. Trap Instants and Sorceries go to Grave after resolving. Trap permanents enter face up. Explicit same-turn permission removes only the one-turn wait.
